name: vedo
role: Scientific 3D visualisation and analysis with VTK and NumPy
summary: Python library and CLI built on VTK and NumPy for loading, analysing and rendering meshes, point clouds and volumes. Its CLI can write images noninteractively, including in explicit offscreen mode; it covers scientific visualisation without requiring a browser scene.
use_when: Render scientific meshes, point clouds or volumes from Python
Produce a static view from a VTK, STL, OBJ or volume input
Add analysis and presentation to mesh data before delivery
avoid_when: Build a complete animated production scene: Blender
Do lightweight triangle-mesh processing only: Trimesh
Render an interactive browser-based VTK scene: vtk.js
license: MIT for project code; bundled fonts have a separate licence and dependencies retain their own terms.
notes: 2026-11-15: listed-in-prd is a legacy schema status for surfaced candidates; it does not mean this tool appeared in the PRD.
2026-11-15: Official documentation demonstrates noninteractive image output and explicit offscreen rendering; server setup examples depend on Mesa/OpenGL and Xvfb.
2026-11-15: Whether offscreen rendering works reliably on macOS arm64 without a window and whether output is repeatable across VTK/OpenGL drivers are unverified.
2026-11-15: Skill opportunity: further research first; no VCR fixture or repeated workflow evidence yet.

assessment.rationale: Official docs establish a Python and CLI route, including noninteractive image output and explicit offscreen rendering. It adds scientific mesh, point-cloud and volume visualization; macOS headless behavior and render reproducibility still need fixture evidence.

evidence.result: Two separate Python processes wrote and reloaded VTP; each preserved 4 points, 2 triangles, bounds [0,2,0,3,0,4], connectivity and point coordinates. Geometry SHA-256 e65e2cc8e13535e9c695f1def112a362c4e55077deb05af4f03a7cdec952765f.
evidence.scope: VTP mesh write/load via Vedo 2026.6.3 and VTK 9.7.2 on macOS arm64; 4 points/2 triangles and bounds preserved; no rendering or other formats/platforms.
